s08.client_chat.cc_001: Dzień dobry. My name is Barbara Kaczmarek and my granddaughter is twelve years old and her mother took her out of Poland on the eleventh of March without telling anybody.
s08.client_chat.cc_002: My son has done everything properly. He went to a solicitor, there is a Hague application, there is a hearing in England on the ninth of June and the court will order her back. Everyone tells me this.
s08.client_chat.cc_003: But the court needs an address and nobody has one, and the solicitor says these things take months, and Zosia is twelve and I have not heard her voice since the tenth of March.
s08.client_chat.cc_004: So I am paying you out of my own money and I have not told my son I am doing it, because he would say I was interfering, and he would be right.
s08.client_chat.cc_005: I have her phone. She left it on her desk, plugged in. I have a key to the flat, I have had one for eleven years.
s08.client_chat.cc_006: It still works. My son kept paying the line, in case. And you should know it is all one family account — the mail, the photographs, the music, all four of their devices on the one login since 2019. Marek set it up. He said it was simpler.
s08.client_chat.cc_007: I am giving you the phone as it is, live, in front of me. Find out where they are. Will you?
s08.client_chat.cc_008: Thank you. Start with her friends. She is never off that chat, that child.
s08.client_chat.cc_009: And I will say one thing now so I do not have to say it later. Whatever her mother has told her about this family, it is not true. Hannah is not a wicked woman but she is not well, and she has never been able to cope here.
s08.interstitial.is1_002: I counted them twice because I did not believe the first count. Thirty-one nights in fourteen months when that child did not sleep in her own bed.
s08.interstitial.is1_003: And on eleven of them she was in my spare room and I made her pancakes in the morning and I never once asked why she was there, because she was there and that was lovely.
s08.interstitial.is1_004: Keep going. I am not going to say anything else yet.
s08.interstitial.is2_002: Evidence. A twelve-year-old opened an album on her telephone and typed the word evidence and started putting things in it.
s08.interstitial.is2_003: I taught her to sew. I taught her the names of the birds on the balcony. Somebody taught her that.
s08.interstitial.is2_004: Go on. I want all of it now, not the kind version.
s08.interstitial.is3_001: Hannah stopped it herself. The procedure. She signed the form asking for it to be discontinued.
s08.interstitial.is3_002: And I have been telling people for two months that if any of it were true she would have gone to somebody, and she did go to somebody, and then she took it back, and I have spent the morning working out why a person does that.
s08.interstitial.is3_003: I rang the doctor. Sikora. She would not discuss a patient with me and then she said one sentence, which was: I am glad somebody is asking.
s08.interstitial.is3_004: Finish it. I want to know where they are and I want to know what I am going to do about it, in that order.
s08.closing_chat.cl_001: Whitby. I had to look at a map. It is on the sea, in Yorkshire, and her mother's sister lives four streets from the harbour.
s08.closing_chat.cl_002: There are photographs from Tuesday. She is on a wall with an ice cream in February weather and she is wearing somebody else's coat and she looks — she looks like herself. That is the thing I cannot get past.
s08.closing_chat.cl_003: Now. I am going to lay out what I understand and you can correct me, because I have been getting things wrong for two years and I would like to stop.
s08.closing_chat.cl_004: The law is on my son's side. That is not an opinion, the solicitor has explained it three times. She took the child, the child's home is Kraków, the court sends the child back. The reason a court can refuse is grave risk, and the burden is on Hannah, and Hannah has one doctor, one teacher and a procedure she withdrew.
s08.closing_chat.cl_005: And she has a telephone that she does not know exists, belonging to a child who wrote the word evidence on an album.
s08.closing_chat.cl_006: The address is the whole case. If it goes to Reder it goes to the court and there is an order and it is executed and Zosia is back in Kraków inside a month.
s08.closing_chat.cl_007: So there are three things I can do and I have been sitting here since six o'clock this morning with a cup of tea I have not drunk.
s08.closing_chat.cl_008: One. Give Reder the address. It is what I hired you for. It is what my son is entitled to and he is my son and I have not slept either.
s08.closing_chat.cl_009: Two. Tell him you found nothing. He will believe me, because he has never once considered that I might lie to him, and that is its own answer about the two of us.
s08.closing_chat.cl_010: Three. Not the address. The phone. Give the phone to Hannah's solicitors in England, for the hearing, and let a court hear what a twelve-year-old recorded in her own hallway. Marek will know it was me by the end of the week and I will lose him. I want to be clear that I know that.
s08.closing_chat.cl_011: Tell me what to do. I am asking properly.
s08.closing_chat.cl_011.opt1: Give Reder the address. It's what you hired me for.
s08.closing_chat.cl_011.opt3: Send the phone to the hearing.
s08.closing_chat.cl_013: Then he gets it, and it is done properly, and whatever comes after that comes after that.
s08.closing_chat.cl_014: I would like you to know that I did consider the other two for four hours. I want that written down somewhere, even if it is only here.
s08.closing_chat.cl_015: Nothing, then. I will tell him the woman I hired was useless and I wasted my money and he will be kind to me about it, which will be the worst part.
s08.closing_chat.cl_016: It buys her months. It does not buy her anything else and I know that. But she is twelve, and months are not nothing when you are twelve.
s08.closing_chat.cl_017: The phone, then. To the English solicitors, with everything on it, and I will write a statement of my own to go with it.
s08.closing_chat.cl_018: Eleven nights she was in my spare room and I made her pancakes and asked her nothing. If I am going to be in this story at all I would rather be in it saying something.
s08.closing_chat.cl_019: You did the job I paid you for. I want to be honest that I wish, at about question seven, that you had been worse at it.
s08.ending.address:
The address went to Reder on the Monday and into the English proceedings on the Wednesday. The return order was made on 9 June and executed on 3 July. Zosia was back at Szkoła Podstawowa nr 26 for the start of the autumn term, in 7b, at the same desk.

The Article 13(b) defence was argued and it failed, which the judgment records in nine lines. Hannah had one A&E letter, one note from a form teacher, and a Blue Card procedure she had asked to have discontinued herself; the court noted that the withdrawal was 'not adequately explained'. Neither Hannah's solicitors nor the court were aware that the phone existed.

Hannah returned to Kraków in August because there was no version of this in which she did not. She has contact three afternoons a week, supervised for the first six months, at a centre on Krupnicza.

Barbara sees Zosia every Sunday. She writes that the child is fine, that she is doing well at school, that she has got very tall. In the last message she sent she added one line and then a second message saying to ignore it. The line was: she does not play music at night any more, and I do not know whether that is a good thing or not, and I have nobody to ask.
s08.ending.nothing:
Barbara told her son that the investigator had found nothing and that she had wasted eleven hundred złoty, and he was gentle with her about it for a fortnight, which she describes as the hardest two weeks of her life.

Without an address the English court could not serve or list, and the hearing on 9 June was adjourned twice and then relisted for the following spring. Under the Convention, delay is not neutral: once a child has been in a country more than a year, a court may refuse return if the child is settled there. Zosia will have been in Whitby fourteen months by the time it is heard.

Nobody has told her any of this. She started at a school on the West Cliff in September and she is in the choir, which she has never been in before, and her Polish is going slightly to pieces in a way that annoys her enormously.

Marek is still the applicant. He rings his mother on Sundays. He has begun to say that the delay is deliberate and that somebody is helping them, and Barbara agrees with him that it is very strange, and then puts the phone down and sits in the kitchen for a while.

The last thing Barbara wrote was: I have not decided whether I did the right thing. I have decided that I am not going to find out, and that this is the price, and that I will pay it.
s08.ending.phone:
The phone went to England by courier with a four-page statement from Barbara Kaczmarek, in Polish, translated at her own expense.

The hearing ran three days instead of one. The court heard a voice memo of fifty-one minutes recorded on 4 October from a shelf in a hallway in Podgórze, and the transcripts of eleven more, and it heard why a woman withdraws a Blue Card procedure, from a paediatrician who had opened one and been overruled. Return was refused under Article 13(b). The judgment is unusual in naming the album: 'The court has had regard to the material the child herself preserved, and to the fact that she preserved it.'

Marek Kaczmarek has appealed. He has also not spoken to his mother since the eleventh of June and has told his brother that she is not to be given the address of anything.

Prosecutors in Kraków opened a file in the autumn on the basis of the same material. It is going slowly.

Zosia is thirteen. She was not called to give evidence and has never been told exactly what was played in that courtroom, only that her grandmother sent it. She writes to Barbara in Polish, badly and every week, and signs off the same way every time, which Barbara has not translated for anybody and does not intend to.

s08.mail.gm_005.subject: Re: Wniosek — Konwencja haska (draft for approval)
s08.mail.gm_005.body:
Panie Marku,

Draft application attached for your approval before it goes to the Central Authority. Please read the statements at paragraph 6 carefully — you are signing them as true.

  6.1  The child has lived in Kraków since birth and has attended
       Szkoła Podstawowa nr 26 without interruption.
  6.2  The applicant has never been the subject of any child
       protection procedure or investigation.
  6.3  The respondent removed the child from Poland on 11 March 2026
       without the applicant's knowledge or consent.
  6.4  The child's habitual residence is the Republic of Poland.

On 6.2 — you told me on the telephone there was 'a thing at the hospital that came to nothing'. If there is a closed procedure it does not have to be volunteered, but the statement as drafted has to be accurate. Tell me if it needs changing.

T. Reder
s08.mail.gm_006.subject: Re: Re: Wniosek — Konwencja haska
s08.mail.gm_006.body:
Tomasz,

6.2 is fine as it is. It was closed. Nothing was found and nothing was recorded against me. Send it.

M.K.

s08.question.q01.title: Three of them
s08.question.q01.question: There is one group chat she is never out of. What do the three of them call themselves?
s08.question.q02.title: The same question
s08.question.q02.question: Over fourteen months she asks her friends for the same thing thirty-one times, almost always at about nine in the evening. What is she asking for?
s08.question.q03.title: Between two and four
s08.question.q03.question: On the nights she is at home, something plays on this phone between two and four in the morning. She made it herself and gave it a name. What is it called?
s08.question.q03.opt1: Check the play times, not the songs
s08.question.q04.title: By the front door
s08.question.q04.question: In the corner of fourteen ordinary photographs taken in her own hallway across eight months, one object keeps appearing and then going away again. What is it?
s08.question.q04.opt1: Look past what she was photographing
s08.question.q05.title: Two languages
s08.question.q05.question: She writes her notes in Polish — homework, revision, lists. For one particular kind of thing she always switches. Which language does she switch into, and why is the answer the whole point?
s08.question.q05.opt2: Read the first line of it
s08.question.q06.title: Behind the boots
s08.question.q06.question: On 4 October she recorded fifty-one minutes and she is not in the room for most of it. Where did she put the phone?
s08.question.q07.title: She named it herself
s08.question.q07.question: One album on this phone is locked. A twelve-year-old set the code and typed the name. What is the album called?
s08.question.q07.opt1: Find the code in her note of passwords
s08.question.q08.title: The same sentence, twice
s08.question.q08.question: She photographed two hospital discharge sheets, fourteen months apart, and outlined the same three words on both in green pen. What does the reported cause say?
s08.question.q09.title: One of them did something
s08.question.q09.question: The second time, the doctor did not let it go. Under Polish law she started a formal procedure that any clinician, teacher or officer can begin. What is it called?
s08.question.q10.title: Who closed it
s08.question.q10.question: That procedure ran for four months and was then discontinued at the written request of one adult in the household. Which one?
s08.question.q10.opt2: Look at the second sheet under the form
s08.question.q11.title: The last week

s08.question.q13.title: Whose door
s08.question.q13.question: Thirty-one nights she did not sleep at home. Seventeen at Kalina's. On eleven of them she went to one other door, and was let in without ever being asked why. Whose?
s08.question.q14.title: Six words
s08.question.q14.question: There is one instruction from that person on this phone. It is kindly meant and it is the reason none of this was ever said out loud. Who is Zosia told not to tell?
